items.informal_name: A non-zero scalar multiple of an algebraic element is integral
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Ring A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A] {z : A},
  IsAlgebraic R z → ∃ y, y ≠ 0 ∧ IsIntegral R (y • z)
items.informal_description: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$ be an $R$-algebra. If an element $z \in A$ is algebraic over $R$, then there exists a non-zero element $y \in R$ such that the scalar multiple $y \cdot z$ is an integral element over $R$.

items.informal_name: Characterization of algebraic elements over a reduced ring
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} {A : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Ring A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A] {z : A} [IsReduced R],
  IsAlgebraic R z ↔ ∃ y, y ≠ 0 ∧ IsIntegral R (y • z)
items.informal_description: Let `R` be a reduced commutative ring and `A` be an `R`-algebra. An element `z ∈ A` is algebraic over `R` if and only if there exists a non-zero element `y ∈ R` such that the element `y * z` is integral over `R`.

items.informal_name: Existence of Integral Multiples in Algebraic Algebras Over Domains
items.type:
∀ (R : Type u_1) {A : Type u_3} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Ring A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A] [NoZeroDivisors R]
  [alg : Algebra.IsAlgebraic R A] (s : Finset A), ∃ y, y ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ z ∈ s, IsIntegral R (y • z)
items.informal_description: Let $ R $ be a commutative ring with no zero divisors and $ A $ an algebra over $ R $ that is algebraic. For any finite subset $ S \subseteq A $, there exists a nonzero element $ y \in R $ such that $ y \cdot z $ is integral over $ R $ for all $ z \in S $. This means there exists a common nonzero scalar $ y $ that clears denominators to make all elements of $ S $ satisfy monic polynomial equations with coefficients in $ R $.

items.informal_name: Existence of integral multiples for a finite set of elements
items.type:
∀ (A : Type u_1) (K : Type u_2) [inst : CommRing A] [inst_1 : Field K] [inst_2 : Algebra A K] [IsFractionRing A K]
  {L : Type u_3} [inst_4 : Field L] [inst_5 : Algebra K L] [inst_6 : Algebra A L] [IsScalarTower A K L]
  [FiniteDimensional K L] [IsDomain A] (s : Finset L), ∃ y, y ≠ 0 ∧ ∀ x ∈ s, IsIntegral A (y • x)
items.informal_description: Let $R$ be an integral domain with field of fractions $K$. Let $L$ be a finite field extension of $K$. Let $A$ be a subring of $L$ that is also an $R$-algebra. For any finite subset $s \subseteq L$, there exists a non-zero element $y \in A$ such that for every element $x \in s$, the product $yx$ is integral over $A$. An element is integral over $A$ if it is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in $A$.

items.informal_name: Algebraic Elements over a Field are Integral
items.type:
∀ {K : Type u} {A : Type v} [inst : Field K] [inst_1 : Ring A] [inst_2 : Algebra K A] {x : A},
  IsAlgebraic K x → IsIntegral K x
items.informal_description: If an element $ x $ of a ring $ A $ is algebraic over a field $ K $, then it is integral over $ K $. This means that whenever there exists a nonzero polynomial $ p \in K[X] $ satisfying $ p(x) = 0 $, there also exists a monic polynomial $ q \in K[X] $ (with leading coefficient 1) such that $ q(x) = 0 $.

items.informal_name: Integral Elements over ℤ are Integers
items.type: ∀ {α : Type u_1} [inst : DivisionRing α] [CharZero α] {x : α}, IsIntegral ℤ x → ((∃ q, x = ↑q) ↔ ∃ k, x = ↑k)
items.informal_description: For any element $ x $ integral over $ \mathbb{Z} $, there exists a rational number $ q $ such that $ x = q $ if and only if there exists an integer $ k $ such that $ x = k $. In other words, the only rational numbers that are integral over $ \mathbb{Z} $ are the integers themselves.

items.informal_name: Integers are Algebraic over Non-trivial Rings
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u} {A : Type v} [inst : CommRing R] [inst_1 : Ring A] [inst_2 : Algebra R A] [Nontrivial R] (n : ℤ),
  IsAlgebraic R ↑n
items.informal_description: For any non-trivial ring $ R $, every integer $ n $ is algebraic over $ R $ when embedded into an $ R $-algebra $ A $.

items.informal_name: Elements of the Ring of Integers of a Number Field are Integral over ℤ
items.type: ∀ {K : Type u_1} [inst : Field K] (x : NumberField.RingOfIntegers K), IsIntegral ℤ x
items.informal_description: Every element $ x $ in the ring of integers $ \mathcal{O}_K $ of a number field $ K $ satisfies a monic polynomial equation with integer coefficients, i.e., there exist integers $ r_0, r_1, \dotsc, r_n \in \mathbb{Z} $ with $ r_n = 1 $ such that $ r_n x^n + r_{n-1} x^{n-1} + \dotsb + r_0 = 0 $.
